claim: Let \(h,k\ge 2\) with \(h\ne k\). Let \(P=A_1\oplus\cdots\oplus A_h\) be a finite weak order with \(|A_i|=2\) for every \(i\), and let \(Q=B_1\oplus\cdots\oplus B_k\) be a finite weak order with \(|B_j|\ge2\) for every \(j\). Then every continuous map \(f:P\to Q\) is homotopic, as a map of finite spaces, to a constant map. Equivalently, the finite function space \(Q^P\) is path connected. In particular, for the canonical minimal finite sphere models \(X_n=(S^0)^{\circledast(n+1)}\) and \(X_m=(S^0)^{\circledast(m+1)}\) with \(n,m\ge1\) and \(n\ne m\), the finite-space homotopy set \([X_n,X_m]\) is a singleton.

integrity.novelty_boundary: Strengthens prior classical order-complex nullity to finite-space null-homotopy and extends the target from minimal sphere models to arbitrary noncontractible weak orders.
integrity.proof_core: A singleton occupied target level contracts the image; otherwise each binary source level occupies one distinct target level. Height excess forces the singleton case, while height deficit leaves an unused target level that gives a pointwise-comparable contraction of the inclusion.
integrity.verification_scope: Exhaustive map and mapping-component checks on six unequal-height source-target pairs with uniform and nonuniform target levels.

scientific_limitations: The theorem assumes every source level has exactly two points.
Equal-height source and target weak orders are excluded and can have non-null isolated map classes.
The claim concerns direct finite-space homotopy and does not obstruct representation after subdivision or enlargement.
title: Height mismatch nullifies maps from binary-level finite pseudospheres
